title: 17. Version Control (Git)
content:
# 17. Version Control (Git)

Git is the standard for tracking changes in computer files and coordinating work on those files among multiple people.

## Core Concepts

```mermaid
graph LR
    WD[Working Directory] -->|git add| Stage[Staging Area]
    Stage -->|git commit| Repo[Local Repository]
    Repo -->|git push| Remote[Remote Repository]
    Remote -->|git fetch| Repo
    Repo -->|git checkout| WD

    style WD fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:black
    style Stage fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:black
    style Repo fill:#efe,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:black
    style Remote fill:#fdd,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:black
```

## Basic Workflow

1.  **Initialize**: Turn a folder into a Git repo.
    ```bash
    git init
    ```
2.  **Status**: Check what has changed.
    ```bash
    git status
    ```
3.  **Stage**: Prepare files for a commit.
    ```bash
    git add filename.txt
    git add .  # Add everything
    ```
4.  **Commit**: Save the snapshot.
    ```bash
    git commit -m "Added a new feature"
    ```
5.  **Log**: View history.
    ```bash
    git log --oneline --graph
    ```

## Branching & Merging

-   **Create Branch**: `git checkout -b feature-login`
-   **Switch Branch**: `git checkout main`
-   **Merge**: Combine changes.
    ```bash
    git checkout main
    git merge feature-login
    ```

## Remote Repositories

-   **Clone**: Download a repo.
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
    ```
-   **Push**: Upload changes.
    ```bash
    git push origin main
    ```
-   **Pull**: Download and merge changes.
    ```bash
    git pull origin main
    ```

## Deep Dive: .gitignore
Create a file named `.gitignore` to tell Git what **not** to track (e.g., `node_modules/`, `.env`, build artifacts).

## Practice Challenge
1.  Initialize a new repo in a test folder.
2.  Create a file, add it, and commit it.
3.  Create a branch `dev`.
4.  Make a change in `dev` and commit.
5.  Switch back to `main` and merge `dev`.
